solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Show up and trim feathers as required

definitions.meaning: to show someone up is to humiliate them and deflate their pride
literally, to shorten feathers to the length needed

explanation.surface: A bird keeper gets told to turn up and clip the plumage as needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the idiom: humbling a person, or literally reducing something to the right dimensions.

clue.text: Cocoa looked odd — that could be a wake-up call

indicators.note: says the letters of the preceding words could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone's morning cocoa looks strange, which serves as an alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'that could be' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel's crow at dawn is the traditional rousing call that wakes a farmyard.

clue.text: Unusually expansive decay upended trunk

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned upside down means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
decay means rot

explanation.surface: A tree trunk with spreading rot has been toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upended' turns OSROT round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body is its central part without head or limbs.

clue.text: Bail boat out, holding north, with last of tide to be had

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold another letter inside them
bailing out suggests the letters are thrown about and rearranged

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

indicators.note: the final letter of the word tide is taken

explanation.surface: A sailor bails out a boat heading north, catching the end of the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes OBTAIABL from BAILBOAT; 'holding' puts N inside it, and 'last of' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available to be had is something one can get or acquire.

clue.text: Nicked head oozed red

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
oozing red is a playful way to say bled

explanation.surface: A cut on the head bled.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobbled is British slang for stolen or tampered with, as is nicked.

clue.text: Opportunity to be batting first

definitions.meaning: a chance or gap one can take
in cricket, the first pair of batters are the openers

explanation.surface: A chance to bat at the top of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a chance; in cricket the first batters are opening the innings.

clue.text: One's a male Muslim minister

parts.note: One's means one is, said in the first person as I am

explanation.surface: Someone declares that he is a man who serves as a Muslim cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque, the Islamic counterpart of a minister.

clue.text: Leader breaking up ideal trio

indicators.note: a trio breaking up has its letters scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A news story about a perfect threesome splitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' is the newspaper sense, not a person heading something.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leader is its editorial, the article giving the paper's opinion.

clue.text: Clairvoyants seeing bank clerks after large amount of money

indicators.note: the clerks come after the money, so their word follows it

parts.note: a fortune is a large sum of money
tellers are clerks at a bank counter

explanation.surface: Psychics consult the bank staff after coming into a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Clairvoyants claim to see the future, which is what such seers tell.

clue.text: Where happy families brag and patience may be welcome

definitions.text: Where happy families brag and patience may be welcome

parts.words: Where happy families brag and patience may be welcome
parts.note: Happy Families, Brag and Patience are all card games, played at such a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A place where contented households boast and tolerance is appreciated.
explanation.walkthrough: Happy Families is a children's card game; Brag is a British gambling card game; Patience is the British name for solitaire.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding table for playing cards hosts all three of the named games.

clue.text: In the morning I'm off, mate

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon
I'm off means I go

explanation.surface: Someone leaving early in the morning says goodbye to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, a pal or chum.

clue.text: Duck in trouble? Add one garlicky mayo!

indicators.note: the duck is placed inside the trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cook rescuing a duck dish suggests a dollop of garlic sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is the Provençal sauce of garlic emulsified with oil and egg.

clue.text: Den's sleazier now and then

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: taking letters only occasionally means every other one

explanation.surface: A den grows seedier from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den or a hideout.

clue.text: Stampede diverted with surrounding grass cleared

indicators.note: the grass sits around the rest, its letters at both ends
the grass is cleared away, removing those letters

parts.note: diverted means rerouted
reed is a kind of grass

explanation.surface: Cattle stampede onto a different path after the grass round them is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stampede' reads as a verb but is the noun; the grass's letters are split, two at each end of the diverted word, so 'surrounding' and 'cleared' strip both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a disorderly flight, like a stampede of fleeing troops.

clue.text: Old fogey claiming local's an anti-monarchist

indicators.note: the fogey claims, or takes inside, the local

parts.note: a relic is an old-fashioned person
a local is a British person's nearest pub

explanation.surface: A grumpy elderly man at the pub turns out to oppose the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, your 'local' is the pub you regularly drink at.
explanation.definitionFit: A republican wants a state with an elected head rather than a king or queen.

clue.text: Space to grow fruit or veg

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A gardener weighs up a plot for fruit or vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a piece of land planted with fruit trees.

clue.text: Noise on the increase — cut short street party

indicators.note: the street word is trimmed of its final letter

parts.note: a crescent is a curved street
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A street party ends early as the din grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a gradual rise in loudness, in music or otherwise.

clue.text: Germanic cast wanting male from Athens?

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, so the letters are thrown into a new order
wanting means lacking, so a letter is removed

explanation.surface: A German theatre company short of a leading man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' removes M from GERMANIC, leaving GERANIC for 'cast' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Grecian means relating to ancient Greece, whose most famous city is Athens.

clue.text: OK to check the foreign resident

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or restrain, so the article holds the other word in

parts.note: der is German for the
well means OK, in good health

explanation.surface: Checking that a foreign resident is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller is someone who lives in a place, an inhabitant.

clue.text: Duck out of shambolic regional shuffle

indicators.note: shambolic means chaotic, so the letters are jumbled
the duck is taken out of the word

parts.note: a duck is a cricket score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A duck escapes during a chaotic regional reorganisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes O from REGIONAL; 'shambolic' rearranges REGINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to rearrange or regroup, as in a cabinet shuffle.

clue.text: Learner in two-seater touching ton — so brace

indicators.note: touching means next to, so the ton follows directly
the learner sits inside the car

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door, often two-seat, car
L is the learner-driver sign

explanation.surface: A learner driver in a sports car hits a hundred, so braces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ton' is British slang for 100 mph; 'brace' means a pair, not bracing oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of lines, and a brace is a pair.

clue.text: Dave driving? Getting stiff?

parts.note: Dave driving pictures the name sitting inside a car, and a stiff is slang for a corpse

explanation.surface: Is a man named Dave stiffening up behind the wheel?
explanation.walkthrough: Driving puts Dave in a CAR: CA + DAVE + R; 'stiff' is slang for a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a corpse, which in slang is called a stiff.

clue.text: No case for bad-tempered stamp

indicators.note: the outer letters, the case of the word, are dropped

parts.note: tetchy means irritable

explanation.surface: An irritable man is told he has no grounds to stamp his foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave or imprint a design, as one might stamp it.

clue.text: Source of friction in 'Titus Andronicus'

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the play's title

explanation.surface: A row backstage during a staging of Shakespeare's bloodiest play.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit, as on sandpaper, is used to create friction for smoothing.

clue.text: The French state pound is permissible

parts.note: le is French for the
GA is the abbreviation for Georgia, a US state
L stands for libra, a pound

explanation.surface: In France, the national currency is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legal is allowed by law, hence permissible.

clue.text: Articulate fellows in front

indicators.note: articulate means spoken clearly, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: guys are fellows

explanation.surface: Eloquent men standing at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise or front is an outward appearance concealing the truth.

clue.text: Inflated claim coming from British tabloid

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: An exaggerated story appears in a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A brag is a boast, an exaggerated claim about oneself.

clue.text: Proprietor on the other hand covering everywhere but south

indicators.note: the outer word covers, or encloses, the inner letters

parts.note: or introduces an alternative, like on the other hand
all compass points except S leaves W, N and E

explanation.surface: A business owner who covers every region except the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points W, N, E stand in for everywhere, in the order the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a proprietor, the person a property belongs to.

clue.text: Sarcasm is lazy? No answer — instead it's very English

indicators.note: no means the answer letter is dropped
something else goes in its place

parts.note: inactive means idle
V for very and E for English

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether sarcasm is lazy and gets the reply that it is typically English.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the A in INACTIVE for VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Invective is abusive, cutting language, of which sarcasm is a form.

clue.text: Heart pounding's caused by them? They're the ones you want to talk to!

definitions.meaning: whimsically, grinders of an organ such as the heart would pound it

definitions.text: They're the ones you want to talk to!
definitions.meaning: from the saying talk to the monkey's master, not the monkey, meaning the person in charge

explanation.surface: A racing heart, and the people worth speaking to.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'talk to the organ grinder, not the monkey' means deal with the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Street musicians with barrel organs; the idiom makes them the bosses one should address.
